independent: isolated codex exec; no sibling votes or Claude vote in context
reasons: The two cited lines are not clean false positives under the stated N5 purpose. They do more than identify a circuit case as superseded; they teach the SCOTUS disposition/holding inside Recent developments, including the Supreme Court reversal and the search-question result.

The proposed suppression would hide true positives. A line can mention a circuit provenance before a SCOTUS tag while still being a SCOTUS Recent-developments violation, e.g. a SCOTUS case described as coming from the 9th Cir. before saying SCOTUS held something.

Keeping has_us untouched does not save this fix because the lint only inspects the 45-character window after the first case name. In the provided lines, the later 609 U.S. cite and SCOTUS holding can sit outside that window, so suppressing has_tag can erase the only current signal.

window[:tag.start()] is not a sound semantic boundary. It misses circuit context before the matched case name, while a broader whole-line scan would create even more masking risk for real SCOTUS entries that mention lower-court history.
residual_risks: The current lint may be detecting these examples for the wrong immediate token, but the line-level violation still appears real.
There may be genuine provenance-only mentions of 'superseded by SCOTUS' that deserve lower-noise handling, but this proposed exception is too broad.
suggested_tightening: Do not suppress solely because a circuit reference precedes a SCOTUS token. Instead classify whether the line contains a SCOTUS case/cite or holding language anywhere in the Recent-developments entry; only consider a narrow provenance-only exception when there is no later SCOTUS case name, reporter cite, or holding/disposition language.
